Breathe through anything. (Especially the hard stuff.)

Learn how your nervous system works, how trauma shapes it, and which breath to reach for when your system is running too hot or too flat. Six live classes and 21 three minute practices you keep for life: a first aid kit you carry in your own body.

Taught by Esther Kalaba, Registered Psychotherapist, with 20 years of clinical practice, much of it in trauma work.

$495 CAD. Six live 90 minute classes on Zoom, plus practices you keep.

“I’m exhausted, on edge, and I can’t switch it off.”

If that’s you, I want you to know something first: there is nothing wrong with you. Your body is doing exactly what it was built to do. When you’ve been running on empty for months, or holding on to something that happened to you years ago, your nervous system does what it can to keep you safe. You feel wired and tired at the same time. You snap at the people you love, or you go numb and can’t get off the couch. None of that means you are broken.

I’ve been a psychotherapist for 20 years, and I’ve spent much of that time working with people who have experienced trauma. Here’s what I’ve seen: trauma doesn’t stay in the past. It shows up in your relationships, in how close you let people come, in how quickly you react, in how hard it is for you to trust or to rest. It shapes your capacity to show up at work, with your family and in your own life, in ways you’d never connect to what happened.

And so many people blame themselves for how trauma makes them feel. I want you to put that blame down. Learning how your nervous system works is not a luxury. Of everything I teach, it’s as close to essential as it gets. Understanding it reduces shame, builds compassion for yourself and puts you back in the driver’s seat.

Therapy can help you make sense of what happened. Your breath is one of the simplest ways to help your body, mind and emotions settle. That’s why I created the Nervous System First Aid Kit: simple practices you can use alongside therapy and any healing work you’re doing, whenever you need them. You can stop waiting and start taking charge.

You are not your stress.

Esther Kalaba, MA, RP

who it’s for.

For anyone running on empty, and the people who care for them.

  • Emotional burnout
  • Mental fatigue
  • Chronic stress and overwhelm
  • Nervous system depletion
  • Trauma symptoms or a history of trauma
  • Anxiety or trouble settling
  • Health care practitioners
  • Therapists and yoga teachers

New to breathwork? This course assumes you know long and deep breathing and Breath of Fire, so we recommend Begin with Breath first.

do you need to calm, balance or energize?

Dose your breath like medicine.

Every nervous system is different, and so is every day. The kit gives you three pathways, 21 three minute practices in all, with guidance on when to use each one, so you can choose the breath your body needs right now.

  • The Calming Series

    to slow down

    Practices that activate the parasympathetic nervous system, slow your breath and restore a sense of peace. For when you’re wired, anxious or can’t settle.

  • The Balancing Series

    to steady yourself

    Daily practices that build emotional resilience, lung capacity and mental stamina, so the next hard day doesn’t knock you over.

  • The Energizing Series

    to come back to life

    Breathwork to uplift, awaken and focus the mind, so you feel more clear, present and alive. For when you’re flat, foggy or frozen.

how it works.

Learn it. Practice it. Choose it. Share it.

  1. Learn.

    Stress is biology, not a personality flaw. Once you understand your nervous system, you can work with it, not against it. You are not your stress.

  2. Practice.

    Theory is great. Practice is better. Every tool takes about three minutes: like brushing your teeth, but for your brain. You’re breathing anyway. Let’s make it conscious.

  3. Choose.

    Calm, balance or energize. You learn which breath to reach for and when, so you can dose it like medicine.

  4. Share.

    Breathwork isn’t just for you. It’s for your family, your co-workers, your friends, even strangers. Those who breathe together, stay together.

six weeks, six live classes.

The six week syllabus.

Each class blends yogic breathwork, somatic therapy and psychoeducation, so you understand what stress and trauma do in the body, and you practice the tools that help.

  1. Week 1

    Understanding Traumathrough a yogic and somatic lens

    • From “what’s wrong with me” to “what happened to me.”
    • Trauma through psychological, somatic, yogic and cultural eyes, and trauma as undigested experience.
    • Finding safety through movement and self inquiry.
  2. Week 2

    Sensory Awareness and Interoceptiondeveloping inner listening

    • Interoception, neuroception and proprioception.
    • Your personal stress signature, and how you find your way back to calm.
    • Observing experience without interpretation.
  3. Week 3

    The Stress Responseawaken the sympathetic nervous system

    • Your stress response patterns, and what your triggers are.
    • The physiology of hyperarousal.
    • How to discharge stress safely through movement.
  4. Week 4

    Vitality, Fear and the Edge of Growththe antidote to stress is vitality

    • Reconnect with life force energy, prana.
    • The role of courage, chaos and creative risk.
    • Imagine your vitalized self, and name what fuels you.
  5. Week 5

    Hypoarousal, Grief and Depressionworking with collapse states

    • Hypoarousal and the dorsal vagal response.
    • Awareness of the frozen body and mind.
    • Slow, grounding breathwork for downward spirals.
  6. Week 6

    Integration, Relationship and Attunementhealing in connection

    • Why trauma healing is relational.
    • Attunement through movement, breath and mirroring.
    • Knowing your own limits and boundaries.

Questions people ask before they begin.

Anything else? Write to breathe@peopleoftheprana.com.

How does the kit fit with Begin with Breath and BEAT + BREATH™?

BEAT + BREATH™ is where most people start: three minutes a day, set to a beat. Begin with Breath is the foundation, with more than 30 practices and why they work. The Nervous System First Aid Kit is the advanced course, for going deeper into stress and trauma. You can buy Begin with Breath and the kit together as a package and save.

Is the Nervous System First Aid Kit a substitute for therapy?

No. The Nervous System First Aid Kit is breath education, not psychotherapy. Esther is a Registered Psychotherapist, but in this course she teaches as a breath educator: the classes are not therapy sessions, and taking the course does not make you her client. It isn’t a replacement for psychotherapy, trauma treatment or clinical care. It can be a helpful companion to your healing, especially when you’re working with difficult emotions or trauma related material in therapy. Think of it as a self regulation toolkit you can use between sessions, in challenging moments, or whenever you need to ground yourself at home.

Is this course for beginners?

This course assumes you’re already familiar with the foundational breath practices of Kundalini yoga and therapeutic breathwork, especially long and deep breathing and Breath of Fire. If you’re brand new to breathwork or unsure about the basics, we highly recommend Begin with Breath first, which teaches the essential techniques more thoroughly. You can also buy both courses together as a package and save.

What if I’m in burnout and feel like I can’t do anything extra right now?

We get it. This course was designed for people in states of depletion, overwhelm and burnout, which is why every practice is only about three minutes long. The goal isn’t to fix or perform. It’s to gently reconnect you with your body, your breath and your natural rhythms, at your own pace, one breath at a time. Many of the practices can be done lying down in bed.

What kind of results can I expect?

Many people tell us they feel calmer, more focused, grounded and emotionally resilient after a few weeks of regular practice. Others notice changes in their sleep, their mood and how they handle daily stress. This isn’t a quick fix. It’s a practice that supports your nervous system over time, like a security blanket: you’ll have tools to go to in times of stress.

Is breathing safe?

The practices are safe for most people. Please let us know at the start if you have a condition such as high blood pressure, or if you’re pregnant, as there are certain practices we’ll ask you to skip. If a practice brings up more than feels manageable, stop, return to your natural breath and reach out to your care provider. Never practice in water, while driving or while operating machinery.

Can I share this with my clients, family or co-workers?

Yes! You’re welcome to share what you’re learning with others. If you’re a health care provider, educator or therapist and want to bring these tools into your practice or workplace, see our options for professionals and our organizational programs.
